issues.legal_issue: Liability for an offence committed by members of an assembly requires proof that the assembly had a specified common object.
material_facts: The accused were among a group of at least five who were ploughing disputed land when the opposing party arrived and an altercation followed.
The prosecution evidence did not establish that the group had any of the specified common objects, either when it assembled or later.
issues.conclusion: The convictions based on membership of an unlawful assembly could not stand because the prosecution had not proved a specified common object.
issues.legal_principle: Section 149 of the Indian Penal Code requires an assembly of five or more persons with a common object of a kind specified in Section 141, and the commission of an offence in prosecution of that object or one the members knew was likely. Under the explanation to Section 141, an assembly that was lawful when formed may later become unlawful, but the evidence must establish the required common object. No earlier cases are cited.

predicates.criminal_appeal_against_conviction: The accused appealed from convictions entered in a criminal proceeding.
predicates.assembly_of_five_or_more: Five or more accused persons acted as an assembly in the events underlying the charge.
predicates.specified_common_object_not_proved: The prosecution evidence did not establish that the assembly had a common object of a legally specified kind.

issues.definition: When a criminal appeal challenges an assembly-based conviction, an assembly of five or more coupled with a failure to prove its specified common object makes that conviction unsustainable.

issues.legal_issue: A person who directly inflicts a fatal injury with another assailant may be liable for murder committed by them in furtherance of their common intention.
material_facts: Two accused struck the victim on the head with bladed weapons.
The victim died from the blows.
issues.conclusion: The two assailants were guilty of murder with joint liability, and their convictions and life sentences were upheld.
issues.legal_principle: Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code imposes joint liability where a criminal act is done by several persons in furtherance of their common intention. Common intention requires concert and a prior meeting of minds, which may be inferred from conduct and circumstances and may develop during the events. No earlier cases are cited.

predicates.criminal_appeal_against_conviction: The accused appealed from convictions entered in a criminal proceeding.
predicates.multiple_assailants_inflicted_fatal_blow: More than one assailant struck the victim with weapons, and the victim died from the injuries.
predicates.common_intention_established: The conduct or circumstances established that the assailants acted in concert with a common intention to commit the criminal act.

issues.definition: In a criminal appeal, multiple assailants who inflict fatal blows are jointly liable for murder when their common intention is established.

issues.legal_issue: Presence during a fatal attack, including restraining the victim, does not by itself establish common intention to commit murder with later-arriving attackers.
material_facts: Two accused caught hold of the victim.
Other accused then arrived with bladed weapons and struck the victim on the head, causing his death.
The evidence did not establish that the two who restrained the victim had shared a prior plan or common intention with the assailants who delivered the fatal blows.
issues.conclusion: The two accused who caught hold of the victim could not be held guilty of murder on the basis of joint liability and were acquitted of that charge.
issues.legal_principle: Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code requires participation in a criminal act in furtherance of a common intention. A prior concert or meeting of minds must be proved, though it may be inferred from conduct or circumstances and may develop during the events. The mere fact that persons caught hold of the victim before others arrived and attacked him did not establish that common intention. No earlier cases are cited.

predicates.accused_restrained_victim: The accused held or restrained the victim during the incident.
predicates.separate_assailants_later_inflicted_fata: Other persons arrived after the victim was restrained and inflicted the blows that caused the victim's death.
predicates.common_intention_not_proved: The evidence did not establish a prior concert or shared intention between the accused and the fatal assailants.

issues.definition: In a criminal appeal, a person who restrained the victim is not liable for murder with later-arriving assailants when the evidence does not prove their common intention.

issues.legal_issue: A person who fires the fatal shot is individually liable for murder when reliable eyewitness and medical evidence establish that the shot caused the victim's death.
material_facts: An eyewitness consistently identified one accused as the person who fired a gun at the victim.
The victim died at the scene from the gunshot injury.
Medical evidence corroborated the eyewitness account.
issues.conclusion: The shooter was convicted of murder, his life sentence was upheld, and his appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: The court applied the murder provision of the Indian Penal Code to the proved intentional fatal shooting. It relied on consistent eyewitness identification corroborated by medical evidence. No earlier cases are cited.

predicates.eyewitness_account_medically_corroborate: Consistent eyewitness evidence identifying the shooter was corroborated by medical evidence.

issues.definition: In a criminal appeal, an accused is individually liable for murder when the accused fired the shot that caused death and reliable eyewitness evidence is medically corroborated.

issues.legal_issue: An accused who participates with another in causing a knife injury may be convicted for the assault where the evidence establishes their joint participation but not liability for murder.
material_facts: Two accused were found to have caused an injury to the informant with a knife.
The court treated their conduct as causing an injury rather than as participation in either victim's murder.
They had already spent more than seven years in custody.
issues.conclusion: The two accused were convicted of the lesser assault offence with joint liability, sentenced to two years' imprisonment, and directed to be released because they had already served more than that period.
issues.legal_principle: The court applied Sections 324 and 34 of the Indian Penal Code to the joint infliction of a knife injury. It substituted that conviction for the murder-related conviction and ordered release in light of the custody already served. No earlier cases are cited.

predicates.criminal_appeal_against_conviction: The accused appealed from convictions entered in a criminal proceeding.
predicates.accused_jointly_caused_knife_injury: The accused acted together in causing an injury to a person with a knife.
predicates.injury_did_not_establish_murder_liabilit: The evidence established the knife injury but did not establish that the accused were liable for a victim's murder.

issues.definition: In a criminal appeal, accused who jointly caused a knife injury but were not proved liable for murder receive a joint assault conviction instead of a murder conviction.
